close_reason: Added 'Validation' rustdoc section to LocalDateTime, Duration, SignedDuration that explicitly documents the no-validation policy already documented in PLAN.md (parsing left to the backend, to avoid pulling in a heavy date-time parser). The lack of validation is intentional per the crate's PLAN.md design constraint; the fix is making this discoverable from rendered rustdoc rather than only in the PLAN. Considered adding TryFrom variants with full RFC 8984 ABNF validation but rejected: parsing the 4-part LocalDateTime + variable-precision ABNF + the ISO 8601 duration subset is the heavy-parser-dep cost that PLAN.md deliberately defers. Consumers who want strict validation can add a wrapper crate; this crate intentionally stays minimal.
description:
**Contract risk**: `LocalDateTime`, `Duration`, and `SignedDuration`
are newtype wrappers around `String` with `From<String>` and
`From<&str>` impls. None of these impls validates the value
against the format documented in the docstrings:

- `LocalDateTime` says \"Format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS\"
- `Duration` says \"ISO 8601 duration string\"
- `SignedDuration` says \"Like Duration but may be prefixed with + or -\"

But:

    let bogus = LocalDateTime::from(\"not a datetime\");  // succeeds
    let also  = Duration::from(\"\\x00\\x00\\x00\");      // succeeds
    let huh   = SignedDuration::from(\"hello world\");    // succeeds

**What goes wrong for callers**:
- A function signature `fn schedule(at: LocalDateTime)` reads as
  \"give me a valid local date-time\", but the type system enforces
  no such thing. Callers may believe the wrapper enforces the
  format and skip their own validation — the type is acting as a
  false oracle.
- Server-side code constructing these from user input will accept
  garbage and serialize it back to the wire, where a downstream
  client may parse it differently or crash.
- Round-trip preservation tests (and the existing
  `recurrence_rule_until_is_bare_string_on_the_wire` etc.) use
  spec-conformant inputs so they don't surface the gap.

**Defended? Yes — but the defense is split across two files**:
The crate-level doc-comment in `lib.rs` lines 26–27 says
\"Validation of internal format is left to the backend.\" PLAN.md
§\"Scalar wrappers\" repeats it. README §\"Gotchas\" mentions it.
But the per-type docstring (e.g. `pub struct LocalDateTime(String)`
at line 41) does NOT repeat the warning — a caller reading
rustdoc on `LocalDateTime` alone will not see it. Existing finding
JMAP-mno4.3 covers missing Display; this is a separate axis.

**Fix shape** (additive, non-breaking):
Option A: add a `TryFrom<&str>` / `TryFrom<String>` impl that
validates via a vendored ABNF regex, while keeping `From<&str>`
infallible for backward-compatibility. This is the conservative
move.
Option B: repeat the \"validation is the backend's job\" warning
in the per-type docstring so callers reading rustdoc on the
individual type are forewarned. This is the minimum docs fix.

Without one of these, the type's contract is \"looks typed,
isn't\" — a defensive-code-forcing situation for every consumer
who actually wants validity.
title: LocalDateTime/Duration/SignedDuration constructors From<String> and From<&str> accept any string without format validation — type-level intent is unenforceable contract
